slides.title: Why Young Men Are Turning To The Manosphere
slides.subtitle: Simon Squibb on LinkedIn
slides.description: This issue is critical, but if we just complain and vilify young people and the people they look up to, we will not fix the problem. We will only make it worse. It's no secret. Young men need a role model. Women do too. But with the recent manosphere issue, I want to address it one last time. Not just to highlight the problems like Louis's documentary did, but also to provide solutions. I'm a father to a young boy, and I am trying to be his role model, but I'm also realistic. I know that as he grows older, he will also look elsewhere for role models. And as someone with 24+ million followers, many of them young men, I can see the issues young people face and why they sometimes search for a role model in the wrong places. Issue 1: The Lack of Role Models When I was 15, my father passed away. At that time, I also needed a role model. There was a huge lack of supply back then, and I was drawn to the stories of Richard Branson, the excitement of travel and the concept of "enjoying your work." As we see today, Richard's influence on me shaped my entire life. That's how important this issue is. But Richard was pretty much all I had. Without a plethora of positive role models to choose from, at a vulnerable time in my life, I could very easily have been swayed by someone else. If social media had been a thing back then, I could see how someone like Andrew Tate could have taken hold of my life. For the record, I never hate anyone. I'd even be open to a conversation with these people. But Andrew Tate and the get-rich lies they sell and peddle for their own gains really upset me. The annoying thing is that some of what they say is true, about the lack of opportunity for so many (because of the system). But it's the huge lies they sell and misogynistic stupidity they peddle (at scale) that motivates me to be in the arena fighting against their version of a good life. I often feel alone in this battle because many don't actually understand what's happening. Issue 2: The lack of virtues I've noticed that people are often encouraged not to set virtues. And this isn't solely on social media either. It's also been largely pushed by Hollywood and large streaming platforms. Movies like The Wolf of Wall Street, combined with influencers peddling get-rich-quick schemes, encourage selfishness and a lack of boundaries to get to where they want to be. They portray success and money as achievable only through scamming, lying, and degeneracy, when in reality, getting rich is achieved by helping people and doing the right thing. Stories like Patagonia, a billionaire giving away his company to fight climate change, are not shown. Here are my virtues: I have been in love with one woman for the last 25 years. I believe in helping people even when it means you lose money. I believe a person's brand is doing what you promise and treating people right. I never sell courses, scam people or charge for help. I am not perfect, far from it. I've made mistakes I regret, but I always try to do what is right and help people when I can. I also enjoy money and what it can bring, including a nice home and cars, but never at the expense of others. By holding these virtues as absolute, I have made more money than I could ever need. I am rich and famous, the dream most of these influencers sell to these young men. Issue 3: Elders still scoff at influencers Even some of my friends still laugh at the word influencers. They still don't get it, and to change, everyone must understand. Influencers have HUGE power. A whole generation of kids who hang on every word these influencers say. They are swayed in their opinions, actions and virtues. Influencers have just as much (if not more) influence over young people as most parents. And people must understand this, because influence at this scale has been able to cause wars in the wrong hands. The Solution If we want to truly deal with the manosphere, we need to do a few things: 1. Understand the problem, not just explain it. Louis's doc just explained the issue. It didn't deal with it or offer any solutions. When I say "offer an alternative" to the narrative of the likes of Andrew Tate, that is the solution. When young people ask me about Andrew Tate, all I say is, "Take advice from people whose life you want." I don't judge the young people for being interested in Tate and his views. I actually understand it. BUT when I ask them, "So do you want to be under house arrest for the next 5 years and be famous for starting a sex worker service?" They start to think differently. We should frame the stories of these influencers around the reality of their lives, not just let them mislead young men with false perceptions and images. These kids are smart, and once you show them (don't just tell them), they wake up. I have seen it. 2. Write down your virtues. Encourage young people to do the same. When you write down what you stand for, it becomes a lot harder for the lines to be blurred by others. You have a compass. You know when something doesn't feel right. Most young people have never been asked to do this. We should start. 3. Stop telling young people these people are bad. They won't listen. Show them instead. I may not be cool enough for most young men. But my friend, and UFC Heavyweight Champion Tom Aspinall, is. He helped me change a kid's life. I've also recently seen an influencer named Gymskin online helping random strangers on the street and pushing positivity. These people exist. We just don't share them enough. Negativity gets the clicks. That's how the algorithm works. But if we reshare and support positivity, that will rise too. 4. Become the alternative. We cannot simply say these people are wrong and then offer no alternatives. Young people need someone outside of their parents to look up to. If you remove all the manosphere, course-selling scumbags, what's left? Very little. I say going forward, it must be you. Get on TikTok and YouTube. Share your values. Have some influence instead of just moaning about the lack of values in young people. We must offer an alternative to fight back. Will you do it? 5. Stop giving these people oxygen. Andrew Tate was on the front page of the Financial Times yesterday and on every social media page with the Netflix stories. They need this exposure. Instead, the media needs to show the true stories of people doing the right thing. The FT shows Tate in his expensive car, smoking a cigar. Tate then tweets he is on the front page of the FT being "attacked by the elite." We're feeding them. As an influencer myself, I warn you, being an influencer is hugely powerful and in the wrong hands can kill dreams and destroy young people's moral compasses. We must work together to bring more positive role models to young people while blanking the likes of Tate and giving them no further exposure. It's a reward for their bad behaviour, and they won't go away if it continues. Regarding the manosphere and the lack of documentaries highlighting the positive influence, if anyone is interested in creating a documentary that showcases the positivity of good influencers and their stories, please reach out. I will gladly support. Maybe Louis Theroux will also get involved. P.S. I am currently building a community of positive influencers to combat this. I already have some great people involved, and it's happening very soon. Let me know some positive influencers in the comments, and I'll check them out.

headline: Architecting AI Builder Ecosystems at AGI Ventures Canada | 2026 Forty Under 40 | Open to Fractional & Advisory Roles
topSkills: Product Operations • AI Product Strategy • UX & Design Thinking • Community Building • Startup Leadership
about:
I've spent over a decade inside builder communities watching what actually makes them work and what quietly kills them.

My background is in UX, product, and operations. I worked at Sephora, led interaction design at Bank of America where I shipped their first Apple Watch app, founded a startup in XR, and most recently worked with Masterpiece X in operations and product at the intersection of 3D and AI.

But the thread running through all of it is builders. The people who show up, build in public, share what they know, and make each other better in the process.

I co-founded AGI Ventures Canada in Ottawa after joining a small monthly AI meetup and seeing what was possible. What started as a room of builders sharing what they were working on grew into a community of over 1,700 people through word of mouth alone. Along the way we added weekly co-hacking sessions, Canada's first AI pop-up hacker house, hackathons, and a growing applied AI consulting practice that helps Canadian companies adopt AI in a human way.

I call myself an ecosystem architect, not a community builder. The distinction matters. Community is one piece of a much larger puzzle. Ecosystem is the whole thing: the culture, the roles, the partnerships, the invisible infrastructure that keeps builders building long after the event ends.

I believe collaboration beats competition, that the best builder communities are built on observed values not invented ones, and that the most important innovation in tech right now is happening in small rooms, not big companies.

If you build, you belong.

Open to fractional, interim, and advisory engagements in AI ecosystem strategy and platform development.

about:
I'm Sheldon. I'm building Narrative, we grow podcasts and YouTube channels for VCs and investors.

We help investors build trust at scale.

But I've been a creator long before I was a founder.

When I was 10, I couldn't afford an Elgato to record my FIFA gameplay. So I set up my camera behind me and filmed myself and the screen in one shot. Super scrappy, but I just wanted to create.

That love never died. It just shifted. As I grew up, I fell in love with creating businesses:

→ Sold Match Attax at 9 y/o (repackaged them for better house odds). Failed because I cared more about my collection than making money.

→ Sold soda (flavored soda stream) at boarding school. Failed because Coke is just a better product.

→ Bought a toasted sandwich business in High School. Flipped it 3x within a few weeks. Hired my first employee. Failed because I graduated and was forced to sell.

→ Started 5 dropshipping stores. 4 failed. 1 broke even. Biggest lesson: There is no easy business.

→ Started an agency for luxury Real Estate Agents in South Africa. Learned that in a service business, a lack of deal flow is almost impossible to recover from. Some things you have to learn the hard way.

Now? Our team has produced content that's driven 12M+ views, grown channels to 310K+ subscribers, and helped tech companies hit their highest-performing videos ever.

I also build tools with AI (vibe coding is magic).

I built Brew Atlas, a TripAdvisor for specialty coffee, entirely with AI tools. No code. Just vibes. Claude Code, Cursor, Lovable, and stubbornness. Live in multiple cities with multiple internal tools (scrapers, pipelines, the works) powering it.

I'm a Lovable Ambassador. I already couldn't shut up about Lovable. Now I'm just insufferable about it (but credit rich 🤷‍♂️).

If you're raising your first fund and want to share your story, or just want to nerd out about building things, reach out.

about:
As a Lovable Ambassador since early 2026, I actively engage with the community to elevate Lovable's brand awareness. I joined this community because I believe in building legacy — not just for yourself, but through the people around you. Being an Ambassador has given me a space to do exactly that: learn from others who think long-term, and pay it forward to the next generation coming up behind us.
 
By organizing impactful events and fostering meaningful connections, I contribute to aligning our initiatives with the company's mission while representing one of Europe's fastest-growing startups.
 
But my foundation isn't tech — it's hospitality.
 
I've served this industry for over 25 years, from every position you can name. I've opened three restaurants of my own. I've woken up at 2:00 AM to stand in a corner counting inventory. I've sat down with executives to build a new menu for the new season. And I've watched — hundreds of times — as families came together around a table to enjoy life.
 
I was on the other side of that. The service side. And here's the thing that people don't always understand: I enjoyed it just as much as they did. Maybe more. Being part of those moments — that's not work. That's purpose.
 
Even when I was away from my own family, the sense of being part of a team that served a simple but profound purpose — providing exceptional service, especially on a holiday — that made all the difference. And let me tell you, that's not something easy to do. Scaling up perfection? That's definitely not easy. But with the right teams, we did it.

Lama AI (Former Restaurant Systems) lets any hospitality business owner create a "neuron" — an AI brain for their business — that they control entirely through voice!

Major Accomplishment when I coordinated, captured data, transformed them utilizing the tools 365 E5 that I am learning for the last 8 years. That was my first successful model that revaluated and created all necessary systems to capture the data needed to showcase to all stake holders dynamically what they are paying in real time and how much each plate costed them. That was a side project when at the same time I was running the actual restaurant that produces between 4-5 million per year.

Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen - Oversaw operations across seven restaurant locations with critically understaffed teams. Experienced firsthand what happens when multi-unit operations have no personnel infrastructure — the operational chaos that no amount of manual effort can solve. This role crystallized the need for an AI system that can replace the missing middle management layer in SMB operations.

Managed operations at a high-volume, factory-scale restaurant serving 1,400+ covers in a day with over 150 employees. Learned firsthand how a billion-dollar company (Brinker International) scales through rigid, proprietary operational systems — and what happens when you don't have them. The company was adamant that every manager learn and follow their systems exactly, which is how they achieved scale. This experience taught me the power of systematized operations at volume, and also revealed the gap: these systems only exist inside billion-dollar corporations. Small businesses have nothing equivalent. That insight became a core pillar of Lama AI — bringing enterprise-grade operational systems to SMBs through AI.

Found a shuttered restaurant that had been closed for two years, invested approximately $12,000 to renovate and relaunch it with an elevated modern Greek concept. Identified a market gap — every Greek restaurant in the area was stuck in the 1980s — and created a progressive dining experience that stood out. Built it into a profitable operation and sold the business for $150,000. A 12x return on investment in under two years, demonstrating an ability to identify underserved markets, reposition with a fresh concept, and build value quickly.

First corporate role, managing a location within Sunshine Restaurant Partners (SRP), one of IHOP's largest franchise groups with 150+ restaurants. Learned how high-performing franchise systems achieve industry-leading metrics — 17% food cost and 7% labor cost. Beyond managing my own location, I served as the systems architect for the entire district, designing and implementing custom control systems for labor scheduling and budget management across multiple locations. This was my first experience building operational systems at scale — the direct precursor to Lama AI.

My first venture opening a restaurant in the United States — and my biggest failure. Launched right into the 2008 financial crisis, the worst economic environment of my lifetime. Despite bringing a strong concept, the timing was devastating. The business didn't survive. Lesson learned: timing and market conditions matter as much as the product.

Co-founded the first cocktail bar restaurant in Glyfada, one of Athens' most prominent suburbs — at a time when the area didn't have a single cocktail bar. Built and operated it successfully for five years before selling and relocating to the United States. This was the beginning of everything: my first entrepreneurial venture, launched at age 22, with zero systems, zero playbook, and pure hustle. The lessons from building something from nothing in an underserved market directly mirror what I'm doing now with Lama AI — identifying a gap (no digital platform for Greek wedding vendors) and being first to fill it.

topSkills: Artificial Intelligence for Business • Digital Marketing • Destination Marketing
about:
AI doesn't browse hotel websites. It resolves entities.                                                                                                       

It pulls from your website, TripAdvisor, Google, and Booking.com, then checks whether those sources agree on what your property is. When they agree, AI recommends you. When they don't, it chooses someone else. 

I call this the Agreement Problem. I built the diagnostic that measures it.

Skift Megatrends 2026 asked: Will the model remember you? I built the diagnostic that answers. 

I'm the Founder of Hacestek International and creator of AI Reveal Map™, a free diagnostic for boutique hotels and independent properties that shows your R2R Score: how ready your property is to be recommended by ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI. Scan takes 60 seconds.
                                                                                                                                                                                                  
My background spans 30 years across hospitality and travel — airlines, GDS systems, OTAs, destination marketing, and luxury hospitality. Based in Miami. Work in English and Spanish across the Caribbean, Latin America, and the US.

Ready to Recommend™ on Substack → franciahaces.substack.com
 
Try the free diagnostic at https://www.airevealmap.com

If you’re navigating AI strategy or positioning for a boutique or independent hotel I’d love to connect. 

Areas of expertise: AI Recommendation Readiness • Hospitality AI Strategy • Travel & Tourism Marketing • Destination Marketing • Strategic Narrative Development • VibeCodeTravel™ • Ready to Recommend™ • Entity Identity

about:
I am a results-driven Software Engineer with 8+ years of experience building scalable, user-friendly applications using JavaScript (Node.js, React, Vue.js), cloud platforms (AWS, Digital Ocean), and DevOps tools. My career has been defined by a "builder-first" mindset—whether I’m architecting cloud-native ecosystems for the travel industry or developing SaaS platforms for the Kenyan market.
​Currently, as the Digital Support Manager at Kubali Tours and Travel, I am leading the digital transformation of one of Kenya’s premier travel agencies. I’ve moved the needle from manual, fragmented workflows to a centralized, automated platform—integrating global GDS systems, hotel booking engines, and local fintech gateways like M-PESA to drive operational efficiency.

​What I bring to the table:
​Technical Architecture: Expert in JavaScript/TypeScript, Front-end engineering, and DevOps. I don't just design systems; I stay hands-on with the code to ensure high availability, security, and sub-second performance.
​AI & Product Strategy: I specialize in identifying high-friction operational bottlenecks and solving them through "smart logic" and AI-driven automation. I speak both "Developer" and "Stakeholder," ensuring technical roadmaps align with business growth.
​Localized Innovation: Deeply experienced in the East African tech landscape, from navigating regulatory DMVIC integrations to orchestrating multi-channel payment APIs for regional scale.

​I thrive at the intersection of infrastructure and interface—building the robust back-end systems that allow for intuitive, high-converting front-end experiences.
​Core Stack: React, NodeJS, VueJS, TypeScript, PHP, DevOps (CI/CD), and AI/ML Product Integration..

I have led cross-functional teams, launched successful platforms, and integrated cloud features into digital products. My approach combines agile methodologies, technical innovation, and business strategy, ensuring that tech solutions align with market needs.

I am passionate about:
🔹 Building scalable, cloud-native applications
🔹 Optimizing DevOps workflows and automation
🔹 Leading teams and mentoring developers
🔹 Driving innovation in software architecture and AI integration

I am always eager to explore new opportunities, collaborations, and discussions in the intersection of software engineering, cloud computing, and tech leadership.

💡 Let’s connect!

about:
Steven Bartlett is a 33-year-old British entrepreneur, investor in more than 70 companies, speaker, author, and media owner. He is the founder of Steven.com - the creator media company. Through it's podcast creator "label" called FlightStory, they create and scales new media podcast IP and commercialise that IP through brand partnerships, programmatic revenue, events, book publishing, newsletters, e-commerce, and new product development.

He is also the co-founder of thirdweb, a developer platform powering over 100,000 teams to build and launch web3 applications, and FlightCast, a video-first podcast hosting platform used by some of the world’s largest shows.

Steven first gained recognition as the co-founder and CEO of Social Chain AG, a social media marketing and e-commerce company he launched at 21 and took public on a European stock exchange by the age of 27 via reverse merger. Social Chain AG became a globally recognised business with hundreds of employees across London, Manchester, Berlin, New York, and Los Angeles, working with major brands including Amazon, Apple, and Coca-Cola.

Through his Fund and personal investments, he has backed companies including SpaceX, Huel, ZOE, Whoop, MrBeast, Groq, KetoneIQ, Cadence, PerfectTed, and over 60 others - focusing on businesses that improve human health, happiness, and performance.

Steven is also the creator and host of The Diary of a CEO, the world's second most downloaded podcast and the fastest-growing podcast in the world. He is the youngest-ever investor on BBC’s Dragons’ Den.

about:
Microsoft 365 Solution Architect | Lecturer in Applied Computer Sciences | Advocate for AI, Cybersecurity, and Lifelong Learning

As a Microsoft Innovative Educator Expert for +10 consecutive years, I bring a wealth of experience in streamlining digital workspaces, crafting low-code solutions, and enhancing business processes with cutting-edge technologies. My expertise spans Microsoft 365, cybersecurity, generative AI, and digital entrepreneurship, where I bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application.

Currently, I serve as a lecturer in Applied Computer Science at Howest, where I inspire students and professionals alike through innovative masterclasses, workshops, and international collaborations. Whether it’s organizing a ‘Prompt-a-thon,’ hosting AI-focused masterclasses, or delivering talks on business process management, I thrive on empowering others to harness the potential of AI and digital tools.

I am passionate about connecting ideas, technologies, and people. From mentoring young talent to leading unique projects like AI Wine Tasting or facilitating international tech weeks, I aim to make technology accessible, impactful, and relevant to real-world challenges.

When I’m not teaching or developing next-gen solutions, you can find me engaging in community initiatives like Meer Bomen in Roeselare, curating events, or supporting lifelong learning in IT for seniors.

Let’s connect if you share a passion for innovation, education, or technology-driven growth!

headline: Founder & Managing Partner at Trust Fund. Investor in Lovable, Superhuman, Eight Sleep, Liquid Death, Public.com, and 45+ startups. Built Nasty Gal to $100M+. Wrote #GIRLBOSS.
about:
I'm the Founder & Managing Partner at Trust Fund, an early-stage venture fund backing software companies that help people and teams start, manage, and scale businesses. Our founders are killers building painkillers. 

Our LPs include Marc Andreessen, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks, Jeremy Liew, Andrew Chen, Chris Dixon, Jeff Jordan, Ev Williams, Paris Hilton, and Phil Hellmuth. 

Previously wrote an 18-week New York Times Bestseller, #GIRLBOSS, which was adapted into a scripted Netflix series that premiered on Netﬂix, produced by Charlize Theron.  

Started fashion e-tailer Nasty Gal at 22 years old and bootstrapped it to $30 million profitably, raised $60 million from Index Ventures and Thrive Capital, then scaled it to over $100 million in revenue. 

Went on the victory lap and was featured on the cover of Forbes magazine's 2016 America's Richest Self-Made Women issue (returned the dress I wore in the photo) and featured in the Fortune 40 under 40, Forbes 30 under 30, Inc. 30 under 30, and Fast Company’s Most Creative People in Business lists. 

My interests include drinking coffee on an empty stomach, choosing the best seats on commercial aircraft, and harvesting my hard-won experience for the next generation of founders.

about:
I’m deeply passionate about entrepreneurship and the people who build before permission exists. I love delusional confidence and doing too many things

What draws me in isn’t the idea of startups in theory, but the practice of building,  spotting gaps, taking responsibility early, and creating environments where ambitious people can connect, learn, and compound faster together.

What I’ve done so far reflects that obsession:

I’m the founder of Nomad Estate, an early-stage startup rethinking access to real estate investing, solving an issue in a market worth 400B $.

I’m the first Lovable Ambassador in Spain, where I actively connect IE and Madrid-based students with a global builder-first ecosystem. Through this role, I’ve organized panels and competitions that brought international founders and real startup culture directly into the community as well as companies.

I’m a Venture Network Co-president, organizing and hosting high-density conversations with founders, operators, and investors, including YC-backed startups on the topics of AI, International Branding, Real Estate and many more. 9 events, 19 speakers, 1,000+ registrations — all in just 3 months.

I also co-founded and co-host Unmuted podcast at IE, focused on leadership, communication and the psychology behind entrepreneurship.

Academically, I’m a scholarship recipient at IE University and ranked in the top 7% of my cohort, but most of my learning happens through building, curating rooms, and creating proximity between people who should be in the same conversation.

I love testing limits, looking to see where my next one is.

experience.description:
Ubiety develops advanced AI technology, software, and hardware solutions to detect and understand people’s physical presence via wireless devices.

Key achievements:
• Built a product centric organization focused on outcomes and consumer pain points
• Created product vision, strategy, and roadmap across Ubiety's product portfolio of consumer, residential security business providers, internet service providers, and commercial business security.

HomeAware is the first home awareness security system. While conventional systems overwhelm you with motion alerts without context, HomeAware tells you what matters: who's home, who shouldn't be, and when action is needed. No facial recognition, no indoor cameras, no constant monitoring. Just 24/7 protection built on people and presence: know who's home, feel protected without being watched.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Product Manager | Growth, SEO/GEO & AI-Driven Products | Driving User Retention & Customer Engagement
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: October 3, 2023, Sam worked with Anna-Mi on the same team
receivedRecommendations.description:
Anna-Mi is simply one of the best coworkers, mentors and product managers I have ever had the pleasure of working with. She is an absolute asset to any company and product org lucky enough to have her. 

I’ve had the pleasure of working alongside Anna-Mi as a PM for about two years as I first started my journey into product. Anna-Mi was one of the first people to answer all my silly questions, meet with me to explain product processes and pushed me to do things out of my comfort zone. In those two years, I grew from an inexperienced, rough-around-the-edges PM to someone who feels like they can tackle almost any PM obstacle, mainly because Anna-Mi was there to consistently coach, teach and encourage. 

I admire Anna-Mi for so many reasons. I’ll try to list just a few of the hundreds of reasons below:

1) She’s highly analytical: Anna-Mi relies heavily on data to make informed decisions about products. She’s always on-top of the latest micro and macro trends, and combines this with our own data, to make homerun products. She’s a master at collecting user feedback, and brilliantly uses it to make our users happy. 

2) She’s ultra curious: Anna-Mi is one of the most genuinely curious people I’ve ever met. She’s not afraid to ask questions that make the team think differently. She always had ideas or really interesting questions that lead us to think about our product and business in a different way. She always was one of the first people to dig into data to figure out why certain issues or challenges were occurring, the come up with fixes.

3) She’s insanely thorough and prepared: Anna-Mi is by-far the most prepared human being I’ve ever met. She’s on top of her data trends at all times, she’s always got her slide decks filled out with info/data that anyone can read and understand and she makes sure to go above and beyond when filling out tickets and explaining work to both her team and to the wider product/tech org. Her preparedness made the entire team so much more efficient, and always led to effective execution. 

4)She’s highly empathetic: She’s a fantastic people person. She always makes sure to hear different viewpoints and raise up other voices. She understands the human aspect of work and has always been a champion of everyone, but especially mothers and women. It’s very cool to see such her advocate for, and lift up, those around her. 

5) She’s the best at what she does: To me, Anna-Mi is the ideal product leader. She manages to juggle an intense work schedule, being a mother and being a leader so effortlessly. She has a vision, she’s decisive, she’s a well-respected voice in the room and she has tons of experience to lead even the most difficult projects. 

I’ll always be thankful to have crossed paths with Anna-Mi. She is a fantastic example of a leader, and any company would be lucky to have her. I can, without a doubt, say that she will have a profound impact in wherever she goes and whatever she does because she’s just that talented.

With over 10 years of experience in marketing, sales, and product development, I am passionate about building usable products that can drive behavioral change at scale. As the CEO and Founder of thirty3, I lead a team of teams that leverage domain expertise and data literacy through design and technology. My mission is to create innovative solutions that can help organizations and individuals achieve their goals and improve their lives.

At thirty3, I oversee the strategy, vision, and execution of various projects that span across different industries and sectors. Some of the projects that I am proud of include developing a digital platform for a global health initiative, creating a gamified app for a leading financial institution, and launching a social media campaign for a local charity. I use my skills in new business development, key account management, and marketing communications to establish and maintain strong relationships with clients, partners, and stakeholders. I also foster a culture of collaboration, creativity, and learning within my team, encouraging them to experiment, iterate, and grow.

about:
One of my earliest memories is seeing Silicon Graphics workstations in Jurassic Park and thinking: "hey, those are the same ones in my dad's office." That's where I spent school vacations as a kid - rooms where computers cost more than cars, decisions had weight, and where I learned that being good doesn't win rooms. Trust does.

Since then: 20+ years at the executive layer in Shell, Petrobras, Bayer, Visa, ArcelorMittal, BNDES, and others. Across all industries the pattern remains: the tools work, the data is there, the case is clear - but adoption still stops at the door. Procurement cycles, compliance friction, stakeholders who don’t share a language, timelines that outlive the enthusiasm. That’s the gap I work in.

Currently one of Lovable's earliest Ambassadors, focused on making the enterprise layer work in Brazil: institutional onboarding, compliance navigation, and pipeline development in regulated and high-complexity environments. Organized the first three official Lovable Hackathons in the country, built "Lovable Brasil", one of the platform's largest international communities, and open-sourced the operational structure as an international standard at lovablehackathons.com.

Co-founded GenialPrev, a bootstrapped LegalTech operating in Brazil's regulated pension market, where I led the full GTM operation from inception: brand strategy, campaign architecture, and structuring the commercial team. Turned the founding attorney into one of the sector's most recognized voices (1.8M+ YouTube views).
 
Also co-built Gamma Quant from a three-person room into one of Brazil's most significant quantitative finance products through a full M&A exit to BTG/Empiricus (one of Brazil's leading financial groups). I was in the room for all of it: strategy, positioning, negotiation. Regulation isn't the obstacle. It's the terrain.

volunteering.description:
When Brazil's worst environmental disaster hit, help was available — but unfindable. Volunteers didn't know where to go. Donors didn't know where to send things. I helped fix that.

Built riodoce.help in response: a geo-referenced, collaborative platform that centralized and mapped donations, volunteers, and collection points scattered across dozens of dark social channels. Within 72 hours of launch: 577 registered volunteers, 33 partner companies, 256 donation collection points, and 89 proposed local solutions — with national reach from Roraima to Amapá.

Covered by national press, amplified by public figures. What started as emergency infrastructure evolved into a permanent project supporting and funding third-party sustainability initiatives for communities in the affected region.

Third time building crisis coordination infrastructure from scratch — following similar efforts after Santa Catarina (2008), Alagoas and Pernambuco (2010), and the Serrana Region of Rio de Janeiro (2011).

The R$ 574 million program in public infrastructure that started from a R$ 5 sticker.

It all started as a running joke among friends, then a parody campaign mocking Rio's chronically broken roads — visible, shareable, impossible to ignore. No budget, no mandate, no political backing. Just a clear message on the right channel, at the right moment. The city launched a road rehabilitation program STILL RUNNING TO THIS DAY (2026) directly in response to the sustained pressure it generated. Actually they used my logo, and still are :)

The social capital built through Asfalto Liso was later redirected toward emergency relief coordination — mobilizing volunteers and donations for climate disasters in Santa Catarina, Alagoas, Pernambuco, and the Serrana Region of Rio de Janeiro between 2009 and 2011, and of course later in RioDoce.Help (see above).

about:
Before I built products, I saved lives.

For 9 years in India, I coordinated animal rescue operations—responding to emergency calls at 2am, making life-or-death decisions with incomplete information, and managing limited resources to create maximum impact. That's where I learned what empathy really means: understanding needs that can't be verbalized, prioritizing under extreme pressure, and measuring success in lives changed.

Now I'm bringing that same mindset as a graduate student at Carnegie Mellon University (Class of 2026).

My Journey to PM:
I spent 8 years building the foundation - starting in Quality Assurance (learning user empathy and quality mindset), moving to Business Analysis (mastering requirements and stakeholder management), then Consulting (strategic thinking and client relations), and Product and Program Ownership (leading teams and shipping products). Each role taught me to see products from a different angle.

What I Bring:
- Deep user empathy from understanding unspoken needs
- Strategic problem-solving under resource constraints
- Cross-functional collaboration across engineering, design, and business
- Technical fluency: JIRA, Figma, Postman, Azure DevOps, Agile/SAFe

Current Projects at CMU:
Building AI-powered products, prototyping with Agentic AI tools, and exploring how technology can create meaningful impact. Recent work includes an AI semantic search agent for educational video content.

My philosophy: The best products don't just work, they understand. Whether coordinating rescues or building software, it starts with empathy.

Let's connect if you're working on something meaningful.

publications.title: Coopetition and Complexity: Exploring a Coopetitive Relationship with Complexity
publications.description:
Cooperation have in previous research been seen as a negative impact on competition and 
vice versa. This thesis is building on a concept called coopetition in which cooperation and 
competition is studied simultaneously. Coopetition have been studied in terms of the level of 
cooperation and competition. However, we found a possible link between coopetition and 
complexity in previous literature. Thus, the purpose of this study is to explore whether 
complexity can develop an understanding for what organizations within a company group 
cooperate and compete about as well what they want to cooperate and compete about. 
 
The four main cornerstones in the theoretical frame of reference is cooperation, competition, 
coopetition and complexity. We begin by defining these concepts, describing previous 
research and discuss various factors of the concepts. Finally, we further develop the possible 
link between coopetition and complexity. 
For reaching our purpose we study a company group in the travel industry. We are 
conducting unstructured interviews with people at leading positions in the company group. 
Our analysis is done by thematic network analysis in six steps. 
 
The empirical data is coded, basic themes are found and a condensed version of the 
interviews is presented together with a short presentation about the company group. 
 
In the analysis we present two global themes, cooperation and competition. These are both 
derived from the basic themes and organizing themes. The factors of complexity are the 
organizing themes. 
 
Our conclusion is that complexity can categorize wanted and actual cooperation in the 
company group in the sense that complexity has to be lowered for cooperation to exist. 
Regarding competition, we did not draw any conclusion to our purpose due to lack of data. 
However, we find that competition is mainly seen as negative in the coopetitive situation 
studied.

headline: Business Coach & Advisor to Portfolio Entrepreneurs (Owners / Investors in multiple SMEs) | Keynote Speaker
about:
Increasingly my business coaching work is focused on Portfolio Entrepreneurs + HoldCos - individuals who own a meaningful stake in multiple businesses (or aspire to do so). I deliver “Freedom Through Business” - aiming to add $1M+ per year to my clients' portfolios, while also improving their broader life and family goals. 

Practicing what I preach means working with a small number of great clients + companies, while living my family’s dream life.

I live and work as a full-time traveller, alongside my beautiful wife Harmony while we also worldschool our 6yo daughter ‘Flash’.

In 20 years of business coaching I’ve worked at depth with 400+ businesses across 14 countries and created over $1 Billion of revenue growth.

What My Clients Say:
👉🏾 “Nobody understands me like Jacob does.”
👉🏾 “Jacob makes complex things simple.”
👉🏾 “He answers all my strangest questions without blinking.”
👉🏾 “Jacob helps me make the right decisions every time.”

My goal is to live a life so extraordinary that people on social media think I must be lying. I held a Guinness World Record for the longest ever movie marathon. I’ve published 6 books – historical, architectural, a novel, on start-ups, remote work, and encouraging male leaders to embrace more feminine traits. The last two were Amazon best-sellers.
 
The Coach Foundation has twice named me in their “Best Business Coaches in the World” list. I am a Virtual Speakers Hall of Fame Nominee – remember that next time you host an event and want my wit + wisdom from wherever I am in the world.

A life motto is “Sprezzatura”, making something difficult look simple, or as I prefer to define it “Proactive Laziness”. If you can do the most valuable 1% thing right now then the results will reverberate through your life.

If you're not doing the most valuable 1% thing in your business portfolio right now, let's chat.

www.ComoPortfolio.com
www.JacobAldridge.com

As a conference Speaker and MC, my experience includes: The Ecole des Ponts business school (2024), The Family Law Practitioners Association Conference (2019), Happy Lawyer Happy Life Retreat (2018-2024), generationYOU (2016), Key Person of Influence Australia (2014), World Business and Executive Coach Summit (2011), the Email Marketing Summit Australia (2009-15), and business coaching conferences in Australia, the UK and the USA.

I LOVE invitations for business podcasts or media quotes.

currentPosition.description:
As an international business coach, partner and advisor I work with energetic young companies seeking growth. Since 2006, I have worked with more than 400 companies in Australia, the UK, North America and across Asia-Pacific.

Founder and CEO Coaching ensures that you're focusing on the right things in your business and you have support to execute your best ideas.

Coaching Projects average a 20% uplift in either Revenue or Profit (depending on your focus), working with your Leadership team on the strategic design and implementation of Growth Systems, Revenue Systems, and/or Productivity Systems.

Strategy Workshops - from half a day to your multi-day conference or offsite retreat - bring both energy and practical outcomes that ensure they are both memorable and provide you with a return on investment.

Corporate Training allows larger organisations to more rapidly provide their team with insight and improved capability. Ranging from 2 to 10 sessions per Training Program, the most requested topics are Sales & Lead Generation, Productivity & Profitability, and Coaching & Leadership Skills.

My alumni clients and colleagues describe me as the smart and quirky business guy who makes things happen. I bring business experience that impacts both profit and valuation - plus a unique energy borne from the belief that business is best when it's fun.

I've worked with one-person companies and multi-nationals, with most of my experience working with founders of companies from $US1.5 - $US17 million in annual revenue.

The clients who have received the greatest return on their investment are multi-site professional services firms, especially those with international offices seeking a consistent global approach that will deliver commercial and cultural change for the better.

experience.position: Presenter and Host of Blackboard Fridays
experience.description:
Every Bright Idea Starts with Inspiration

As the owner of a growing business, you know that your success is measured not by past milestones but by the future you’re creating today. And yet it’s increasingly difficult to find the time to pause, breathe, and be inspired.

Blackboard Fridays was designed to create that pause, to find a moment each week to truly focus on your business instead of dealing with the demands of working in it.

Over 134 episodes - more than 13 hours, and 100,000 spoken words - my guest presenters and I shared business strategies, frameworks, and approached to help you start up, scale up, step up or sell up. We even had a freakin' Billboard!

Five minutes. Friday mornings. Just me, a Blackboard, and the Future of your business.
www.blackboardfridays.com.au

View the archive at http://businessdepot.com.au/insights/author/Jacob

I spent 2 years as a Director on the businessDEPOT Accounting Board, during which time we achieved consecutive years of record revenue and oversaw the implementation of plans to diversify businessDEPOT into additional professional services and locations.

In 2018, businessDEPOT was named the Xero Accounting Partner of the Year for Australia.

My specific responsibilities also including leading the businessDEPOT Advisory team, presenting at many of our much-loved business events in Brisbane, Australia, and supporting the visibility of our Brand through marketing initiatives including Blackboard Fridays videos which were viewed more than 35,000 times.

Growing "Leadership, Revenue, Reputation and Wealth" for Real Estate Principals and Agency Owners.

If you are an agency owner seeking business growth and a coach or partner to support you, then we should have a chat.

Here’s what I believe and what our clients preach: These 4 elements have always been the ones that separate industry cowboys from those of us creating sustainable, profitable businesses, and they have never been more important than they are for our industry right now.

While Sales Training, Property Management Coaching, and IT systems have never been better...the lack of dedicated, expert support for real estate Principals continues to hold back businesses and impact lives. Real Estate Grow has launched as a business coaching and consulting firm specialising in working with real estate business owners on their vision, their strategy, and the 12 key areas of their business that will help them achieve their life's dream.

In October 2016, the business coaching and advisory side of Real Estate Grow merged with businessDEPOT, where I now have a larger team and a greater range of expertise to continue helping real estate Principals achieve their dreams. In 2018 this formed the backbone of #RealReach.

In 10 years combining my experience with Shirlaws' IP, research, and team-structure, I coached more than 250 organisations:
* Sizes ranged from individuals (now a master franchisor) to Listed international banks
* Industries ranged from real estate to professional services to construction and more
* Delivered results by building Growth Management Systems that cover Infrastructure, Revenue, Asset Extension, and the Culture that underpins and accelerates them all.
* Locations varied as my base moved from Australia to London (2010-2012) and back again, including ongoing activity to support our global Shirlaws businesses in North America, Europe, and South-East Asia

As an experienced coach, I worked with a variety of businesses across different industries and of many sizes. I specialised in helping young, energetic business owners and their teams, usually ranging from $1.5M-$17M turnover, by providing strategic guidance to help them independently achieve their goals.

This focus, and the systems we helped build and implement, shift entrepreneurs from feeling 'anxious and hopeful' into 'relaxed and confident', which also allows for more exciting business expansion work such as the development of scalable intellectual property that creates them recurring income streams.

At various times I held other roles and responsibilities within Shirlaws Group, the most important of which are listed separately. After 10 valuable years, I made the decision with mixed emotions that the best way to achieve my personal vision was to step outside the Group while still maintaining an excellent relationship with those involved.

I Am Lovable shares simple tools that slay the body image, relationship, communication and money fears that stop young women from creating greatness.

My role was to help build the course material, both live and online, leveraging my training and IP development experience, and help kickstart the growth of the business to support our passionate (and lovable) CEO and clients around Australia.
